<reason>B won by separating ease from efficacy: a nationality cap is controllable but does not free family-suitable homes or stop re-letting, while its revenue and domestic-place costs are immediate. B's bed-conditional alternative answered A's immediacy pressure on the same admissions cycle and exposed A's unwillingness to specify housing gains, despite A's strong externalization and discretionary-growth framing. A's clipped turns and evasive A2 also cost execution.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's Rebuttal 2 was decisive: master-leasing or requiring a contracted bed before any new admission gives immediate protection without using nationality, and shows A's under-2% trigger could remain an indefinite revenue cut delivering no measurable family housing.</best_rebuttal>
